text:
Alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak I'm seeing a small p99 spike for short/low-token requests. Dumping telemetry into #perfhogs.
Mona: Yup — noticed it too. KV hit rate dipped ~3% on the same buckets, average batch size for seq<64 dropped from ~8 -> ~5.
Shreya: That smells like a kernel handoff changing execution time and causing premature batch dispatch. If batches are smaller, token budget math will shift and queue admit may start soft-shedding.
Ryan: Can you share the exact timeline? did kernel selector flip thresholds or enable new handoff delay?
Alex: We lowered prefer-latency threshold so seq<48 prefers the latency kernel. Also enabled immediate handoff (handoff_delay_ms=0) to avoid waiting for bigger batches.
Mona: Immediate handoff probably prevents microcoalescing. Combined with tight token budgets it reduces batch assembly time but hurts throughput.
Shreya: Proposal: for short seqs keep a small handoff_delay (e.g., 50-150ms) and bump token_budget targets slightly so queue admit tolerates transient smaller batches. Also one-shot soft 429 ramp to avoid hard fails.
Ryan: I sketched an admit config for a canary:

```
admission:
  token_budget_per_worker: 192
  soft_429_threshold: 0.85
  soft_429_ramp_ms: 200
  kv_prefetch_window: 64
kernel_selector:
  prefer_latency_kernel_for_seq_lt: 64
  enable_handoff_delay_ms: 100
```

Alex: Looks reasonable. Targets: measure p50/p95/p99 latency, batch_size distribution, kv_hit_rate, queue_length, soft_429 rate and total errors.
Mona: Add "avg batch assembly time" and "microbatch counts" too — those will show if handoff delay actually coalesces work.
Shreya: Also capture kernel CPU utilization and per-kernel tail latency. We saw a tiny regression in kernel-hot path CPU p99 yesterday.
Ryan: I'll run a 10% canary on dedicated region with rollback if p99 > baseline * 1.15 OR errors > 0.5% for 5m window. Rolling at 10:30 PT.
Infra-bot: deploy pipeline triggered for canary: infra/canary/admit-config-v8 -> started
Alex: For the experiment, keep kernel hotswap disabled for the canary so we isolate admit changes vs selector changes.
Mona: Good call. We should also run a short synthetic spike test in staging with bursty short requests to detect oscillation.
Ops: FYI — updated incident playbook to include "admit-tone" rollback steps and alert thresholds for soft_429.
Shreya: If canary stabilizes, follow-up roll will enable a gradual handoff_delay reduction from 100ms -> 50ms over a week, monitor kv_hit recovery and batch size.
Ryan: Noted. I'll post canary dashboards link once the run starts and tag folks.
Infra-bot: canary started at 2439991300, traffic=10%, config=admit-config-v8
Alex: Thanks — will watch dashboards. If anyone sees unexpected spikes ping me and @Ryan.
Mona: +1 :thumbsup:
Shreya: adding perf checks to nightly job too.
Infra-bot: canary health checks OK at 2439991780 (no automatic rollback triggered)
